Day 1 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

The Missing Wallet

從人物的行動找出原因與個性

Kevin was on his way home when he saw a wallet near the bus stop. He picked it up and looked inside. There was some money and a student ID card. Kevin thought about what he should do. He could leave the wallet there, but someone else might take it. He decided to bring it to the police station. An officer used the information on the card to contact the owner. About thirty minutes later, a nervous student arrived. She was surprised and happy to see her wallet again. She thanked Kevin several times. Kevin did not get any money for helping her, but he walked home with a smile. He knew that doing the right thing could make someone's difficult day much better.

需要提示時，再看單字與片語
單字意思／例句
wallet錢包
Kevin found a wallet near the bus stop.
owner物主；主人
The owner was happy to get her wallet back.
decide決定
I decided to ask the teacher for help.
contact聯絡
Please contact me after school.
nervous緊張的
She felt nervous before the test.
  • on one’s way home：在回家的路上
  • pick up：撿起；拿起

1 · 細節理解 · 基礎

Why did Kevin take the wallet to the police station?

  1. He wanted its money.
  2. He wanted to find its owner.
  3. He missed his bus.
  4. He knew the officer.

2 · 細節理解 · 基礎

How did the officer know whom to contact?

  1. From the student ID card.
  2. Kevin told the officer.
  3. The owner called first.
  4. There was a phone in the wallet.

3 · 推論判讀 · 基礎

What can we learn about Kevin?

  1. He expected a reward.
  2. He was afraid of the owner.
  3. He chose to help a stranger.
  4. He wanted to keep the wallet.

4 · 字義推測 · 基礎

Detective: What does “owner” mean in this story?

  1. The person who drives the bus.
  2. The person the wallet belongs to.
  3. The officer at the station.
  4. The person who sells wallets.

5 · 推論判讀 · 進階

Why was the student probably nervous before arriving?

  1. She was buying a new wallet.
  2. She disliked the officer.
  3. She had missed a school show.
  4. She did not know if she could get her wallet back.

6 · 主旨統整 · 挑戰

Which sentence best expresses the message of the story?

  1. Helping others can be rewarding without money.
  2. Police stations are always near bus stops.
  3. Student ID cards are more valuable than money.
  4. It is best to leave lost things where they are.

Day 2 · 日常生活 · 10 分鐘

A Lunch Worth Sharing

抓住問題、轉折與解決方式

Mia opened her lunch box and sighed. Her father had made vegetable rice again. She wanted to buy a sandwich, but she had left her money at home. Across the table, Leo was drinking water. His lunch box was still in his schoolbag.

“Are you not hungry?” Mia asked. Leo looked down. “I forgot to pack lunch this morning.” Mia remembered that her father always gave her more rice than she could finish. She moved her box to the middle of the table and asked Leo to get another spoon.

As they ate, Leo told her a funny story about his dog. Mia laughed so hard that she almost dropped her spoon. The rice tasted the same as yesterday, but lunch felt different. That evening, she asked her father to teach her how to cook it. Next time, she wanted to make enough for two.

需要提示時，再看單字與片語
單字意思／例句
share分享
Mia shared her lunch with Leo.
pack裝好；打包
Remember to pack your lunch.
finish吃完；完成
I cannot finish all this rice.
spoon湯匙
Leo got another spoon.
enough足夠的
We have enough food for two.
  • leave something at home：把某物忘在家裡
  • so ... that ...：如此……以至於……

1 · 細節理解 · 基礎

Why couldn’t Mia buy a sandwich?

  1. The shop was closed.
  2. She had no money with her.
  3. Leo wanted the last sandwich.
  4. Her father told her not to.

2 · 細節理解 · 基礎

What did Mia ask Leo to get?

  1. A schoolbag.
  2. Some rice.
  3. Another spoon.
  4. A sandwich.

3 · 推論判讀 · 基礎

Why did lunch feel different to Mia?

  1. She enjoyed sharing food and a conversation.
  2. Her father used a new recipe.
  3. She finally bought a sandwich.
  4. She ate in a new classroom.

4 · 字義推測 · 基礎

Detective: What does “pack lunch” mean?

  1. Pay for a meal.
  2. Throw food away.
  3. Eat very quickly.
  4. Put food in a container to take with you.

5 · 推論判讀 · 進階

What will Mia most likely do in the future?

  1. Stop eating with Leo.
  2. Prepare lunch to share.
  3. Ask Leo to buy all her meals.
  4. Throw away her lunch box.

6 · 主旨統整 · 挑戰

How does Mia’s attitude toward her lunch change?

  1. From proud to angry.
  2. From excited to afraid.
  3. From disappointed to thankful and interested.
  4. From nervous to bored.

Day 3 · 對話／訊息 · 10 分鐘

The Message Before Practice

比對訊息中的時間、地點與條件

[Class group chat, Friday afternoon]
Amy: The music room is being painted, so tomorrow’s band practice will be in Room 204. Please meet there at nine.
Ben: Does everyone need to bring a music stand?
Amy: No. There are stands in the room. Bring your instrument and the new music sheets.
Max: My bus does not arrive until 9:10. Should I skip practice?
Amy: Of course not! Come as soon as you can. We will start by checking our instruments. The full band will play at 9:20.
Ben: Can we leave our bags in the hallway?
Amy: Please keep them under your chairs. Other students need to use the hallway.
Max: Got it. I will tell Lily about the new room. She cannot check her phone today.
Amy: Thanks! Practice ends at eleven, and we will return the room to the way it was before we leave.

需要提示時，再看單字與片語
單字意思／例句
practice練習
Band practice starts at nine.
instrument樂器；儀器
Please bring your instrument.
hallway走廊
Keep the hallway clear.
skip略過；不參加
Max does not need to skip practice.
return使恢復；歸還
Please return the room to its original state.
  • as soon as you can：儘快
  • not ... until ...：直到……才……

1 · 細節理解 · 基礎

Where will the band practice on Saturday?

  1. In the hallway.
  2. At the bus stop.
  3. In the music room.
  4. In Room 204.

2 · 細節理解 · 基礎

What should Ben bring?

  1. An instrument and new music sheets.
  2. Paint and chairs.
  3. Only a music stand.
  4. Lily’s phone.

3 · 推論判讀 · 基礎

Why does Max offer to tell Lily about the new room?

  1. Lily is painting it.
  2. Lily cannot check her phone today.
  3. Lily is driving his bus.
  4. Lily wants to cancel practice.

4 · 字義推測 · 基礎

Detective: What does “skip practice” mean?

  1. Practice twice.
  2. Play more quickly.
  3. Not attend practice.
  4. Move the chairs.

5 · 細節理解 · 進階

Which plan follows all of Amy’s instructions?

  1. Bring a stand only and put bags in the hallway.
  2. Meet at 9:20 in the music room.
  3. Leave at eleven without checking the room.
  4. Meet in Room 204 and keep bags under chairs.

6 · 推論判讀 · 挑戰

If Max arrives in Room 204 at 9:15, what is true?

  1. He is late for meeting time but early for full-band playing.
  2. He has missed the whole practice.
  3. He must wait outside until eleven.
  4. He arrives before everyone was asked to meet.

Day 4 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

The Mystery of the Wet Cup

用實驗線索分清觀察與解釋

On a hot afternoon, Noah filled a glass with ice water. A few minutes later, the outside of the glass was wet. “Is there a tiny hole?” he wondered. His sister Emma wiped the glass with a towel. Soon, small drops appeared again.

Emma put an empty glass beside it. That glass stayed dry. Then she explained that the air around them contained water vapor, a form of water they could not see. When the vapor touched the cold glass, it cooled and changed into liquid drops. The water on the outside came from the air, not from inside the glass.

Noah wanted to test the idea. He placed a metal spoon in the refrigerator, took it out later, and watched. Drops formed on the spoon too. There was no water inside the spoon to leak out. Noah smiled. Sometimes, a small question at home can lead to a useful experiment.

需要提示時，再看單字與片語
單字意思／例句
vapor蒸氣
Water vapor is present in the air.
liquid液體的；液體
The vapor changed into liquid drops.
appear出現
Small drops appeared on the glass.
contain含有
The air contains water vapor.
experiment實驗
Noah tried a simple experiment.
  • change into：變成
  • lead to：導致；帶來

1 · 細節理解 · 基礎

Where did the water on the outside of the glass come from?

  1. The towel.
  2. A hole in the table.
  3. The air around the glass.
  4. Ice that fell out of the glass.

2 · 細節理解 · 基礎

What happened to the empty glass beside the cold one?

  1. It stayed dry.
  2. It broke.
  3. It became full of ice.
  4. It leaked water.

3 · 推論判讀 · 基礎

Why did Noah use a cold metal spoon?

  1. To stir the water.
  2. To dry the towel.
  3. To make a hole in the glass.
  4. To test whether water could appear without leaking.

4 · 字義推測 · 基礎

Detective: What does “formed” mean in “Drops formed on the spoon too”?

  1. Disappeared.
  2. Appeared or developed.
  3. Became warmer.
  4. Were wiped away.

5 · 推論判讀 · 進階

Which condition is important for the drops in the story?

  1. The object must have a hole.
  2. The room must be dark.
  3. The object is cold enough to cool nearby water vapor.
  4. Someone must pour water onto the object.

6 · 主旨統整 · 挑戰

Which order best describes Noah’s investigation?

  1. Noticing a problem, hearing an explanation, testing it.
  2. Testing a spoon, breaking a glass, buying a towel.
  3. Explaining a result before noticing anything.
  4. Reading a book and copying its answer without testing.

Day 5 · 公告／資訊閱讀 · 10 分鐘

One Ticket, Two Choices

比對活動時間、價格與報名限制

GREEN WEEKEND AT RIVER PARK
Join us this Sunday! All activities begin at the information desk. Children under twelve must come with an adult.

9:00–10:00 | Bird Walk | $80 per person
Borrow binoculars and look for birds with a guide. The group is limited to twelve people. Book online by Friday.

10:30–12:00 | Reuse Workshop | $60 per person
Turn an old T-shirt into a shopping bag. Bring a clean T-shirt and scissors. No booking is needed, but seats are limited.

SPECIAL OFFER
Buy a Bird Walk ticket and join the Reuse Workshop for just $20 more. The offer is for the same person on the same day.

Please bring your own water bottle. If it rains heavily, the Bird Walk will be canceled and its ticket money returned. The workshop will still take place inside the visitor center. Check the park website at seven on Sunday morning for updates before leaving home.

需要提示時，再看單字與片語
單字意思／例句
guide嚮導；指引
A guide will help visitors find birds.
limited有限的
Seats in the workshop are limited.
book預約
Book your Bird Walk ticket online.
offer優惠；提議
This offer is for the same person.
cancel取消
Heavy rain may cancel the walk.
  • take place：舉行；發生
  • per person：每人

1 · 細節理解 · 基礎

What must a visitor bring to the Reuse Workshop?

  1. Binoculars and a ticket to the Bird Walk.
  2. A clean T-shirt and scissors.
  3. A new shopping bag.
  4. A bird guidebook.

2 · 資訊整合 · 基礎

How much does one person pay for both activities with the special offer?

  1. $60.
  2. $80.
  3. $140.
  4. $100.

3 · 細節理解 · 基礎

What happens if it rains heavily?

  1. Both activities move to Monday.
  2. The workshop is canceled.
  3. The Bird Walk is canceled, but the workshop continues inside.
  4. Everyone gets a free ticket.

4 · 字義推測 · 基礎

Detective: What does “book” mean in this notice?

  1. Reserve a place.
  2. Read a story.
  3. Write a report.
  4. Borrow an item.

Day 7 · 單字與錯題復活 · 10 分鐘

The Second-Try Club

用文章證據修正答案，整理一週收穫

Every Sunday, four friends met online for their Second-Try Club. They did not bring new test papers. Instead, each person chose one question they had answered incorrectly during the week.

This week, Ben shared a notice about a park event. He had chosen the wrong starting time because he read only the first line. Amy asked him to find the line that supported his answer. When he checked the notice again, he noticed that two different activities had different times.

Next, Mia showed them a word she had forgotten. She wrote a short sentence about sharing lunch, and the others guessed its meaning. Everyone made a new sentence using the word.

At the end, they each answered their old question again without looking at the answer key. “Getting it wrong was not the end,” Ben said. “It showed me what to check next time.” They agreed to meet again the following Sunday.

Day 9 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

The Invisible Road of Ants

理解螞蟻如何利用氣味訊號選擇並改變路線

Have you ever watched ants move in a line toward a piece of food? An ant that discovers food does not call its friends. On its way back to the nest, it leaves a chemical scent called a pheromone on the ground. Other ants can detect the scent with their antennae and follow the trail. When they find the food, they add more scent as they return. A shorter path is usually traveled more often, so its scent becomes stronger. This helps the group choose an efficient route.

However, the scent does not last forever. It gradually fades. If the food is gone or a path becomes unsafe, fewer ants use that trail, and its signal weakens. The colony can then switch to another route. This simple system has inspired computer programs that compare many possible paths. Ants do not need a leader or a map; repeated small actions allow the whole colony to solve a problem together.

Day 11 · 每週 Boss · 10 分鐘

Boss: The Ice-Cup Challenge

整合實驗步驟、數據與討論，判斷證據能支持到什麼程度

THE ICE-CUP CHALLENGE

[Experiment plan]
Four students wanted to learn which covering slowed ice from melting. They placed equal masses of ice in four identical cups. Each cup was wrapped with one layer of a different material: paper, cotton cloth, aluminum foil, or nothing. All cups stood on the same classroom table. After thirty minutes, the students measured the melted water.

[Results]
Paper: 32 mL
Cotton cloth: 18 mL
Aluminum foil: 24 mL
No covering: 40 mL

[Team discussion]
Mina: Cotton cloth produced the least water, so it kept the ice coldest.
Leo: Yes, under these test conditions. We should not claim that cloth is always best.
Kai: Why not?
Leo: We tested only one layer in one classroom. Sunlight, material thickness, or a longer test might change the result.
Mina: Then our report should include the exact numbers and the limits of our test.
Kai: Next time, let's compare the materials in sunlight and shade, but keep the cup type and amount of ice the same.

Day 12 · 單字與錯題復活 · 10 分鐘

The Five-Card Word Rescue

利用上下文證據複習近期單字，並練習說明修正答案的理由

At the community center, Ms. Lin placed five clue cards around a room. Each card used a word from the week: follow, gradually, reserved, claim, or exact. Teams had to read mini-situations and carry the right word to a final message.

First, Zoe read, “The light became weaker little by little.” She chose gradually. At another station, Ken saw a library book with a student’s name and picked reserved. The hardest clue said, “Do not say something is always true after one small test.” Ken first chose exact, but Zoe asked him to look for evidence. He changed it to claim.

When all five cards were placed correctly, the letters on their back sides formed FOCUS. Ms. Lin did not simply mark wrong choices. She asked each team to explain which words around a blank supported its answer. Before leaving, students rewrote one confusing clue in their own words. Their goal was not to memorize five definitions for one night, but to build a method they could follow in future reading.

Day 13 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

The Extra Point

分辨發現錯誤、修正行動與公平理由。

Every Monday, Amy counts the points for her class reading game. Students earn one point for each book report. This week, her friend Ben gives her two reports, but Amy writes three points beside his name. Ben notices the extra point during lunch.

At first, he says nothing. His team is only one point behind the leaders. Then he remembers the rule they all agreed on: every point needs a finished report. He tells Amy about the mistake before the final scores go on the classroom wall.

Amy thanks him and changes the number. Their team does not win that week, but the game stays fair. On Tuesday, Ben brings another report. This time, he knows exactly why his team receives its next point.

Day 14 · 日常生活 · 10 分鐘

Two Loaves at the Door

On Tuesdays, Leo usually collects a loaf of bread for his grandmother. Today, a delivery worker leaves two bags outside her door. Each bag holds one loaf and a note with the same order number. Grandmother paid for only one loaf.

Leo wants to open both bags because he is hungry. His grandmother asks him to check the order first. He calls the bakery and reads the number aloud. The baker checks her list and explains that a new worker packed the order twice.

She asks Leo to keep one bag sealed. A worker will collect it before four. Leo puts it on a shelf away from the lunch table. When the worker arrives, Leo hands it back. His grandmother cuts their own loaf, and they share it with some soup.

Day 16 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

A Fair Test Needs a Record

區分實驗觀察、推測與紀錄的限制。

Nora’s science group wants to compare two paper towels. They pour ten spoonfuls of water onto a tray and use one sheet to soak it up. Then they repeat the test with the other brand.

The first towel leaves one spoonful on the tray. The second leaves three. Nora writes these numbers in a table. Her partner says, “Let’s write zero for our favorite brand. It will look better.”

Nora refuses. A useful record shows what happened, not what the group hoped would happen. She also notices that their sheets have different sizes. Perhaps the larger towel takes up more water simply because it is larger.

They decide to test equal-sized pieces next time. For now, their report includes the measured amounts and the size difference. It does not name one brand as the winner.

refuse拒絕

Borrow It, Bring It Back

CLASSROOM TOOL SHELF

Our class now shares rulers, scissors, and colored pencils. You may borrow one item at a time. Write your name, the item, and the borrowing time in the blue notebook. Return the item before the last class of the same day begins.

If an item is damaged, tell Ms. Chen before returning it. Do not place it back without a note. Reporting damage does not automatically mean you must pay for it. Ms. Chen will first find out what happened.

The shelf is closed during lunch because the room is used for quiet reading. Tools needed after lunch must be borrowed earlier or after the reading period ends.

Boss: The Class Fund Puzzle

[Class fund record]

[Messages]
Nina: We are $20 short. Did anyone borrow money?

Nina: I can see it now. Next time, please record the purchase immediately.
Jay: I will. Should I put another $20 in the box?
Nina: No. The string was for our project. We need to update the record, not collect the money twice.

[New rule]
Before putting a receipt in the folder, the buyer must enter the date, item, and amount in the notebook. Another student checks the entry against the receipt.

At Friday’s review club, each team receives five cards. The words are extra, sealed, private, permission, and receipt. Teams must match them with short situations, then explain their choices to another team.

Day 20 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

The Ten-Minute Gap

讀懂時間順序，判斷短空檔適合完成的任務。

After school, Eva has ten minutes before her bus leaves. She usually spends them looking through short videos. By evening, she often feels that she has no time for English.

On Monday, her teacher gives the class a small experiment: choose one short task for a waiting period. Eva puts five word cards in her bag. At the bus stop, she looks at each English word, recalls its meaning, and checks the back. She keeps the difficult cards at the front for another try.

She does not try to finish all her homework there. A noisy bus stop is not a good place for every task. At home, she uses her desk for longer reading. After a week, Eva still has busy evenings, but she no longer thinks every waiting minute must be wasted.

Day 21 · 日常生活 · 10 分鐘

Dinner Before the Deadline

利用開放時間與準備時間倒推行動。

Sam promises to return a neighbor’s cake pan before seven tonight. His family also plans to eat dinner at six thirty. He thinks there is plenty of time and begins a computer game at five forty.

At six ten, his mother asks whether the pan is clean. Sam checks the kitchen and finds it beside the sink, still sticky. Washing and drying it takes fifteen minutes. The neighbor lives a ten-minute walk away.

Sam pauses the game, cleans the pan, and leaves at six twenty-five. He reaches the neighbor’s door at six thirty-five. The pan is returned on time, but Sam misses the beginning of dinner.

After eating, he changes tomorrow’s task list. Instead of writing only the final deadline, he adds the time needed to get ready and travel. He also leaves a little room for unexpected delays.

Day 23 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

The Bell and the Puzzle

從實驗紀錄理解中斷、比較與證據限制。

Mr. Wu gives two groups the same kind of word puzzle. Group A works in a quiet room. Group B works in another room, where a bell rings every two minutes. When it rings, those students must stop and write a number before continuing.

Group A finishes after eight minutes. Group B takes eleven. Several students in Group B say they need time to remember where they stopped. Mr. Wu asks whether the bell is the only possible reason for the difference.

Judy points out that the groups contain different students. Some may already be better at word puzzles. The class plans another test with fresh puzzles of similar difficulty. Each group will try the other room.

Their first results suggest that interruptions may matter, but they do not prove that every short break makes every student slower.

Thirty Minutes in the Maker Room

MAKER ROOM BOOKING

The maker room opens from 3:00 to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays. Each team may book one thirty-minute slot per day. Available starting times are 3:00, 3:30, 4:00, and 4:30. Cleaning is included in your slot, so leave the tables ready for the next team.

Book by noon on the day before your visit. For a Monday visit, book by noon on Friday. A booking is complete only after you receive a confirmation message. Writing your name on a waiting list does not reserve a place.

If you arrive more than ten minutes late, the room manager may give your slot to a waiting team. Arriving late never moves the ending time. Bring your design on paper because the room computers are not available for drawing plans. You may use them only to control the machines.

Boss: The Library Window

[Saturday plan]
Noah wants to finish a history poster and return library books. The library closes at 4:30 p.m. He needs ten minutes to walk there, five minutes to return the books, and ten minutes to walk home.

[At 3:00 p.m.]
His poster still needs forty minutes of work. His friend suggests doing it first and then watching a twenty-minute video together. Noah also wants ten spare minutes before the library closes in case the return desk is busy.

[Two choices]
Plan A: Poster, video, then library.
Plan B: Poster, library, then video.

Noah draws a timeline. Under Plan A, he would reach the library at 4:10 and finish at 4:15 if nothing goes wrong. Under Plan B, he would finish returning books at 3:55. Both plans fit the closing time, but only one gives him more than half an hour after the planned return to handle trouble.

Day 26 · 單字與錯題復活 · 10 分鐘

Five Words, One Better Plan

透過新情境複習時間字詞，區分完成與熟悉。

Sophie makes a review sheet with five words: recall, deadline, latest, pause, and delay. She writes a short school story and leaves spaces where the words should go. Then she asks her brother to try it.

The story describes a student who checks an old meeting message, arrives at the wrong room, and loses ten minutes. Sophie’s brother chooses latest for the message the student should have checked. He uses delay for the lost time.

At another space, he first puts deadline after “Please stop the recording for a moment.” Sophie asks him to explain his choice. He changes it to pause and writes a reason beside the sentence.

They do not mark a word as learned just because it looks familiar. The next morning, they cover the answer list and try to recall all five words from new clues.

Day 27 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

One Bowl, Twelve Cups

分辨容器容量、供應份量與公平分配。

At the class food fair, Mina brings a large bowl of fruit salad. Twelve students want to try it. A sign beside the bowl says “One cup for each visitor.” Mina expects the salad to fill twelve small cups.

The first visitor picks up a large drinking cup and prepares to fill it. Mina stops him to explain the intended portion. The sign does not explain which cup to use, and several kinds are sitting on the table.

She places twelve matching small cups beside the bowl and adds a drawing of one to the sign. A classmate moves the large cups to the water table.

Now each visitor gets a similar portion. Mina learns that a rule can sound clear while leaving an important detail unstated. Next time, she will show the serving cup before the fair begins.

The Bigger Bag Is Not the Better Deal

A bright sign above the larger bags says “Family Pack.” Yuri first reaches for one because a bigger package often looks like a better deal. Then she checks the price per apple. In the small bag, each apple costs $15. In the large bag, each costs $16.

Her father asks which bag fits their plan. Yuri chooses the small one. It costs less per apple and provides exactly the number they need. She keeps the $70 difference for another purchase. A package name can catch the eye, she thinks, but it cannot do the calculation for you.

Same Juice, Different Labels

For a class project, Bella pours apple juice from one carton into two identical cups. She marks one “New Recipe” and the other “Regular Recipe.” Five classmates taste both without seeing the carton. Three choose the new recipe, one chooses the regular recipe, and one says they taste the same.

After the tasting, Bella reveals that both cups contain the same juice. Her classmates are surprised. She explains that this small activity cannot tell them exactly why each person chose a cup. The label may have influenced a choice, but chance or the order of tasting could also matter.

Next time, Bella plans to use simple letter labels and change which cup people taste first. Her report includes all five responses, including “the same.” She does not claim to have discovered a new, better juice.

The Recipe Card Repair

For Sunday review, Tess makes a pretend café menu for her younger cousin. She writes five words on separate cards: portion, cost, confirm, recipe, and ingredient. Her cousin must match each word to a short situation.

One situation shows a list of steps for making soup. He selects ingredient because he sees vegetables in the picture. Tess asks him to read the words beside the picture. The clue describes the whole set of instructions, so he changes his choice to recipe.

Next, a server asks a customer to repeat an order before sending it to the kitchen. Her cousin chooses confirm and explains that the server is checking the details.

Before finishing, they write a new clue for portion without drawing any food. Tomorrow, Tess will hide the five cards and ask him to supply the words himself. Pictures can help, but the written clues still matter.

A Sign at the Wrong Gate

On Monday, Owen volunteers to welcome visitors to the school book show. The show is in the library, beside the east gate. A small printed map tells visitors to enter through the north gate and follow the covered path.

Before the show opens, workers close the north gate to repair its steps. Owen puts a sign on the closed gate: “Please use the east gate beside the library.” However, visitors arriving at the bus stop still follow the old maps toward the north gate.

His teacher asks where people first decide which way to walk. Owen returns to the bus stop and places an updated direction sign beside the map board. He also tells the welcome team about the change.

Now visitors learn about the closure before choosing a route. Owen keeps the sign at the north gate too, for anyone coming from another direction.

Day 35 · 日常生活 · 10 分鐘

The Ticket for Two Rides

依實際搭乘次數比較票價，分辨確定與可能行程。

On Tuesday, Hana and her father visit a nearby town. At the bus station, Hana compares two tickets for her own travel. A single ticket costs $40 and covers one ride. A day pass costs $90 and covers any number of rides until the last bus that evening. Tickets cannot be refunded.

Her plan has two rides: from the station to the museum, and from the museum back to the station. She may also visit a riverside market, but she has not decided. That stop would require one additional ride.

Hana buys a single ticket for the first ride. At the museum, rain begins, and she decides not to visit the market. She buys another single ticket for the return journey.

She spends $80 altogether. A day pass would have cost less for three rides, but not for the two she actually takes.

Day 37 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

Seeds on Two Shelves

從實驗紀錄區分改變條件與共同條件。

In a classroom activity, students put ten bean seeds on wet paper in each of two trays. They place one tray on a shelf near the window and the other inside a dark cupboard. Both places feel equally warm.

Every morning, they add the same amount of water and count new roots. After three days, eight seeds in each tray have roots. Mei is surprised because she expected the dark tray to remain empty.

The teacher asks the class to record what they actually see. These seeds began growing in both places. That observation does not show that light never matters. The class has only watched the first few days.

For the next week, they will measure the young plants and note changes in their leaves. They keep the water schedule unchanged so they can compare the trays more carefully.

Day 40 · 單字與錯題復活 · 10 分鐘

The Word Desk Switch

將本週字詞放回語境，依線索修正理解。

Five cards wait on the review desk: label, entrance, record, collect, and preparation. Each pair must place a card beside a short situation. The teacher asks students to explain their choices before turning the cards over to check the answers.

One situation describes a student writing down how many seeds have roots. Another describes a visitor taking a repaired bag home. Hana first puts collect beside the seed situation because she imagines collecting seeds from the ground.

Her partner points to the words writing down. Hana moves record to that situation and collect to the bag situation. They put entrance beside a door description and label beside a paper with a name on it.

The final situation describes sorting materials before the real job begins. After choosing preparation, the pair writes a new example together. They learn that a familiar word still needs to fit the action described around it.

Day 41 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

A Quiet Welcome

以人物行動推論需要，避免替他人做決定。

When a new student joins Class Nine, Max volunteers to welcome her. He plans to introduce Lina to everyone during lunch and asks the class to crowd around her desk. Lina smiles, but she speaks very little and holds her lunchbox tightly.

Max thinks she does not like the class. His teacher suggests asking a simple question instead of guessing. During break, Max asks whether Lina would prefer a busy table or a quiet place for her first lunch.

Lina chooses the quiet table near the window. She explains that she wants to learn a few names at a time. Max invites just two classmates and asks them to speak slowly when explaining the school schedule.

By Friday, Lina is eating with a larger group. Max realizes that a warm welcome does not have to be a loud one. Giving someone a choice can help more than planning a surprise for them.

The Receipt in the Pocket

On her way home, Nora buys a notebook for sixty dollars and a pen for twenty. She pays with a hundred-dollar note. The cashier gives her ten dollars in change and puts the receipt inside the notebook before serving the next customer.

Nora notices the problem outside the shop. She checks the prices on the receipt before returning to the counter. It lists one notebook, one pen, and a ten-dollar gift bag. She did not buy or receive a gift bag.

The cashier checks the items and apologizes. The bag was left on the screen from a canceled purchase. He removes that charge and returns ten dollars to Nora. She thanks him for explaining what happened.

At home, Nora keeps the receipt for a week because the notebook has a return policy for printing problems. The store accepts such returns within seven days, but only if the customer shows proof of purchase.

Day 44 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

A Paper Plane Record

以平均與重複測試判讀資料。

During a classroom challenge, two teams fold paper planes from identical sheets. Team Red folds wide wings, while Team Blue folds narrow ones. The same student launches every plane from one marked line inside the gym, where the doors remain closed.

Red's plane travels four, six, and five meters in three trials. Blue's travels eight, two, and five meters. A student points to Blue's eight-meter flight and calls it the clear winner. Another student asks to compare all three flights first.

Both sets of distances add up to fifteen meters. Their average distance is therefore five meters. Red's results are closer together, although this small test does not tell the class which design will always fly farther.

The students write every result on the board, including the shortest flight. For the next test, they plan more trials with several planes of each design. A single exciting result should not erase the rest of the record.

The Refill Bottle Notice

REFILL WEEK AT THE SCHOOL CAFE: From Monday through Friday, bring a clean reusable cup for a five-dollar discount on hot tea. The regular tea price is thirty dollars. The offer does not apply to bottled drinks or cold fruit juice.

For safety, cups must have a firm base and hold at least three hundred milliliters. Staff may refuse cracked or dirty cups. If your cup is unsuitable, you can buy tea at the regular price in a cafe cup.

The discount is for one drink per student each day. Bringing two cups does not double it. Ask for the discount before paying; staff cannot change a completed payment later because the daily total is recorded automatically.

The water station beside the cafe remains free for everyone. You do not need to buy tea or bring a school card to use it. Please keep the station clean and avoid blocking the walkway while filling your bottle.

A Parcel for the Next Door

依地址與聯絡方式處理誤送物件。

A parcel arrives while Theo is helping his grandmother at home. The label shows their building number, but the apartment number is 5B. They live in 5A. The delivery person has already gone downstairs by the time Theo notices the difference.

Theo wants to open the parcel to find a phone number inside. His grandmother suggests reading the outside label again. It includes the receiver's name and a number for the delivery company. Opening another person's parcel is not needed to report a wrong address.

They call the company and explain the two apartment numbers. The company asks them to keep the parcel unopened until a driver returns. Theo puts it on a dry shelf inside their home, away from the door where someone might trip.

An hour later, the driver collects it and gives them a receipt. Theo's grandmother keeps that receipt until the neighbor confirms receiving the parcel. Checking a small detail has prevented a much larger mix-up.

Day 51 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

Reading a Shadow Log

依觀察表判斷變化，區別紀錄與推論。

A science club makes a shadow log in the schoolyard. Students place one upright stick in a flat patch of ground and mark its position so it will not move. They measure its shadow at nine, eleven, one, and three on a clear day.

The recorded lengths are sixty, thirty-five, thirty, and fifty centimeters. At each check, they also draw an arrow showing which way the shadow points. The teacher asks them to keep the stick and the measuring method the same throughout the activity.

Yuri first writes that the shadow keeps getting shorter all day. Her partner notices the last measurement. Fifty centimeters is longer than thirty, so the sentence does not describe all four observations. Yuri corrects it before handing in the report.

The club plans to repeat the activity on another clear day. They will compare the records without assuming that every date produces exactly the same lengths. Their log describes this stick, this location, and these particular times.

The Timetable Detective

練習先找時間關係，再解釋選項。

The review club creates a short puzzle with the words slot, afterward, directly, separate, and remain. A student reads this instruction: Put the tools away after painting, then return the key to the office. Everyone must explain which action happens first.

Rui chooses afterward for a blank describing the cleanup. She almost selects directly for another blank about storing lunch money away from bus money. Her partner asks whether the sentence is about a route or about keeping two things apart.

Rui changes directly to separate. The group then uses directly for a trip to the office with no stop elsewhere. A booked thirty-minute period is a slot. The last sentence asks how many minutes remain before the bus leaves.

Each student writes one question that could trick a hurried reader. They exchange questions and underline time words before answering. The club's goal is to notice relationships between actions, not simply recognize words from the same week's lessons.

Day 55 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

The Poster with No Names

從同意與修改流程理解作品分享。

A class wants to display drawings from its art project in the school hallway. Jess collects everyone's pictures and begins a poster with each artist's full name underneath. She thinks names will make the display feel more personal and celebrate everybody's work.

One classmate asks to use a nickname instead. Another is happy to show the drawing but prefers no name at all. Jess worries that different labels will look untidy. The teacher suggests asking each artist how they want their work identified.

Jess makes three choices on a form: full name, nickname, or no name. She also asks permission to display each drawing. A student may keep a drawing out of the hallway without losing credit for completing the class project.

The final poster uses labels of the same size but different naming choices. Jess adds a small card inviting visitors to enjoy the artwork. She discovers that a shared display can look organized while still respecting individual decisions.

Day 56 · 日常生活 · 10 分鐘

The Sweater on the Line

追蹤處理衣物的步驟與事後修正。

Leo helps with the washing on Sunday. He places all the clean clothes on the line, including his sister's wool sweater. The sweater is heavy with water, and its sleeves stretch lower than the shirts beside it. His sister notices before leaving for basketball.

She checks the care label inside the sweater. It says to dry the garment flat. She explains that the label gives instructions for this particular item. The instructions on the cotton shirts do not automatically apply to the sweater too.

Together, they move the sweater onto a clean towel on a flat drying rack. Leo writes a small reminder and clips it above the washing machine. He does not write all clothes dry flat; he writes check each care label first.

A week later, Leo washes another load and sorts the items by their care instructions. He finishes a little more slowly, but nobody has to move wet clothes twice. The reminder helps because it directs him to information instead of making an oversized rule.

Day 58 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

The Towel Drying Test

找出實驗中的混淆條件與改善方法。

Three students want to compare drying times for two kinds of cloth. They wet one cotton square and one thick towel, then hang both in the classroom. The cotton square is small, while the towel is four times larger and holds much more water.

After an hour, the square feels dry and the towel is still damp. One student announces that cotton always dries faster than every towel. The others ask whether the test really compared just the material, since several conditions were different.

They decide to try equal-size pieces and add equal amounts of water. They will hang them side by side in the same room and check both at fixed intervals. They also plan to repeat the test before making a stronger statement.

The first result still belongs in their notebook. It describes what happened to those two wet objects. However, it cannot by itself show which single difference caused the drying times. A better question leads to a fairer comparison.

Boss: A Lunch Order That Fits

LUNCH MENU: Rice boxes cost fifty dollars each; vegetable wraps cost forty. Every rice box contains chicken. Wraps contain no meat. Orders of four hundred dollars or more receive free delivery. Smaller orders have a thirty-dollar delivery fee, with no other charges.

They order Ken's combination and write each student's choice beside their name. The food stand confirms the final amount, including delivery, before accepting payment. Ana saves the message so the class can compare the received meals with what it actually ordered.

Day 61 · 單字與錯題復活 · 10 分鐘

A Better Way to Keep Notes

使用具體線索複習字義與避免重複錯誤。

After a week of practice, the reading club reviews five words: purpose, damp, exchanged, exactly, and combination. Instead of copying each meaning five times, students write one short situation and underline the words that make the meaning clear to another reader.

Yun describes a towel that still feels a little wet. Her partner chooses damp. For exchanged, she writes about giving one ticket and receiving one book. A sentence about precisely eight meals helps the pair choose exactly rather than combination.

The combination card goes beside a description of rice boxes together with vegetable wraps. The last situation asks why a photo was taken, so its blank needs purpose. Each student checks whether a different card could fit just as well.

One ambiguous sentence is rewritten before the club keeps it in the review folder. The teacher explains that a useful practice question should contain enough clues for one best answer. Students leave with five situations they can explain, not only five translations they can repeat.

Day 62 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

The Team Behind the Scoreboard

辨別被看見的成果與幕後貢獻。

After a school quiz competition, the winning team poses beside the scoreboard. The school website names the four students who answered questions on stage. Tessa is happy for them, but she notices that three classmates who prepared practice cards are missing from the report.

She asks the teacher whether the team may add a short thank-you note. The teacher agrees, provided every named student is comfortable appearing on the website. Tessa checks with the helpers before writing anything, and one asks to be thanked without a name.

The revised report keeps the original score and the names of the stage players. It adds a sentence thanking two named helpers and one classmate who prefers to stay unnamed. It also describes their work preparing questions and checking answers.

At the next meeting, the team divides jobs before practice begins and records who wants public credit. Tessa learns that accurate recognition includes both what people did and how they wish their contribution to be shared.

Day 63 · 日常生活 · 10 分鐘

The Last Seat at the Salon

從候位與服務長度安排日常時間。

At a small hair salon, Dani asks for a haircut before meeting her aunt at noon. It is eleven ten. The stylist says the next appointment starts at eleven forty, but a simple haircut can fit into the empty half hour if Dani is ready now.

Dani also wants a wash and a careful new style. Together, those services would take fifty minutes. The stylist explains that accepting the longer request now would delay the customer who already booked eleven forty. Dani cannot reserve someone else's time by arriving earlier.

She chooses the simple haircut, which takes twenty minutes, and plans the new style for another day. Before sitting down, she confirms that the price is for the haircut alone. The stylist writes the service and price on a small card.

Dani finishes at eleven thirty and has time for the ten-minute walk to meet her aunt. She is pleased that the salon explained the choices clearly. A free chair does not always mean a worker has an unlimited opening.

Day 65 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

Counting Sounds Carefully

辨認主觀評估與測量限制。

In a listening activity, students try two homemade boxes around the same ticking clock. One box is lined with cloth, and the other is empty. A listener sits one meter away and raises a hand whenever a tick is heard during thirty seconds.

With the empty box, the listener reports twenty ticks. With the lined box, the listener reports eight. The group writes that fewer ticks were reported in the cloth condition. They do not claim that the clock itself ticked more slowly.

The listener might miss sounds for several reasons, including attention and other noise in the classroom. To improve the activity, the group invites several listeners to repeat both conditions. They keep the distance and the listening time unchanged.

Their teacher asks them to separate what happened in the clock from what happened in the listening task. A report of hearing less is useful evidence, but the method and its limits must travel with the number when students explain the result.

  4. Twenty.

  3. The lined box was tested for an hour.

Borrow a Costume, Return a Set

核對借用清單、歸還與污損處理。

COSTUME CUPBOARD: Students may borrow a costume for a school performance with a teacher's signature. Each set has a coat, a hat, and a fabric belt. Check all three pieces at pickup and tell the cupboard volunteer immediately if anything is missing.

Borrowed sets must return by four on the school day after the performance. Do not wash them at home. Some fabrics need special treatment, so the school arranges cleaning. Place any damp piece in a separate open bag and tell the volunteer about it.

The borrower receives a numbered checklist. Keep it until the complete set has been checked back in. A teacher's signature allows borrowing, but it does not replace the final item check. Unreturned pieces remain listed under the borrower's name.

For fittings, visit the cupboard during Wednesday lunch. Fittings do not reserve costumes. A reservation becomes official only when the signed form is accepted. If two students want the same set, the first completed reservation has priority.

Day 68 · 單字與錯題復活 · 10 分鐘

The Card with Two Possible Answers

辨識含糊題幹並用補充線索改善。

The review group uses the words optional, attention, priority, usable, and spare. Their first sentence says that a costume is still in the cupboard. Both spare and usable seem possible, because the sentence does not explain its condition or whether anyone needs it.

Jules rewrites it: This undamaged coat is being kept as an extra in case another one tears. Now spare is the best choice. Another sentence describes an unbroken hat that an actor can wear, making usable the useful answer there.

For priority, the group writes about the first completed reservation being handled before later requests. Optional describes yogurt that a student may leave out. Attention fits a listener focusing carefully so that quiet ticks are less likely to be missed.

The teacher praises the added clues and asks students to explain why the old sentence was weak. Knowing a word's meaning is not enough if the question gives too little information. The group saves both versions to remember how the improvement worked.

Day 69 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

The Question Nobody Asked

以重述確認分工，區分聽見與理解。

During a group project, the teacher asks students to prepare a short talk about a local landmark. Half the group nods while the instructions are read. Everyone looks busy afterward, but their notes do not match when they meet at the end of the period.

Sora has researched the landmark's history. Tim has drawn a detailed map of every bus stop nearby. Mei has written a speech about her favorite restaurant beside it. Each student believed a different detail was the most important part of the assignment.

The group rereads the task card. It asks for the landmark's history, why residents value it, and one practical visiting tip. They can use Sora's research, shorten Tim's map to one useful route, and ask Mei to interview a resident instead.

Before dividing the remaining work, each student repeats their task in their own words. They agree on a two-minute limit for the whole talk. Nodding was quick, but checking a shared understanding turns out to save more time.

Day 70 · 日常生活 · 10 分鐘

A Different Kind of Gift

由行為與回應推論禮物的意義。

Yara wants to give her grandfather a birthday present, but she has little money left after buying school supplies. She considers a cheap mug from a shop. Then she remembers that he already has a cupboard full of mugs and rarely uses the newest ones.

At dinner, her grandfather mentions an old box of family photos he cannot easily sort alone. Yara asks whether he would enjoy organizing them together on Saturday. He agrees and says he would like to tell her who appears in each picture.

Yara brings blank cards and writes the names and dates he remembers. When he is unsure, she marks the card with a question instead of guessing. They make a small album with clear labels and leave the uncertain photos in a separate envelope.

Her grandfather calls the afternoon his favorite part of the birthday weekend. Yara still makes a paper card, but she no longer worries about the missing mug. She has given time to something he actually wanted to do.

Day 72 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

Remembering Shapes in Order

區分測驗順序效應與單一因素結論。

In a memory activity, students see six shapes on a screen for ten seconds and then draw them from memory. They first work in silence. Next, they try a new set while a song plays. Many students remember more shapes during the second round.

Jin writes that music improved everyone's memory. His partner points out that the second round also came after practice. The shapes were different too, and the class did not check whether one set was easier to remember than the other.

The teacher proposes a new comparison. Half the students will begin with music and half without it. Then they will switch conditions. The group will use matching sets prepared in advance and record each student's results separately.

The activity is still small, so the final report will describe these students and these tasks. Jin keeps his original guess in a different section from the results. Seeing a pattern is a useful start, but it is not the same as explaining its cause.

Printing Without Surprises

STUDENT PRINTING DESK: Black-and-white printing costs one dollar for each printed side. Color printing costs five dollars per side. A sheet printed on both sides contains two printed sides, so double-sided printing saves paper but does not change the charge per printed side.

Send your file before two for pickup after three on the same school day. Files received after two are ready the following school day. Include your name, class, number of copies, and whether you want color. Staff will print in black and white unless color is requested.

The desk can staple documents of up to twenty sheets at no extra cost. Larger documents are returned unstapled. Check the page order in your file before sending it; the desk does not rearrange sections or remove blank pages automatically.

If you notice a printing error caused by the desk, bring the entire document back within two school days. If the original file contains the mistake, a corrected reprint is charged as a new job.

Day 75 · 單字與錯題復活 · 10 分鐘

The Page, the Sheet, and the Side

以語境區分相近單字和計數單位。

For review, the club uses five words from its recent tasks: beforehand, separately, side, cover, and submit. Their teacher folds three sheets into a small booklet and asks students to count sheets first, before discussing how many sides could contain writing.

Min says that a cover is always a printed page. Her partner opens a blank notebook and points to its plain outer cover. They decide that the word describes an outside part, while printed describes whether something has been placed on a surface.

A second puzzle asks students to prepare equipment before recording. They choose beforehand. Results kept in different rows are recorded separately. For the last blank, a student must send a finished file to the printing desk, so the group chooses submit.

The class writes a reminder above the counting exercise: identify the unit before calculating. A correct multiplication can still produce the wrong answer if the numbers refer to different things. They test their own examples by asking a partner to explain the units aloud.

Day 76 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

The Helpful Note That Grew Too Long

依讀者目的選取重點，辨識資訊優先順序。

Although Mara knows the science task well, her partner has missed two classes and needs a quick guide before the experiment. Mara writes two full pages describing every discussion, including jokes and the history of how the group chose its topic.

Her partner thanks her but still asks which materials to bring and what to do first. Mara realizes that a complete account of the past is not necessarily a useful set of instructions. The guide needs to answer the reader's immediate questions.

She rewrites it with a materials list, three numbered actions, and a warning to ask the teacher before touching the hot container. Background information moves to the end under a clear label. Her partner can now prepare without searching through the entire story.

Mara keeps the longer notes for the final report, where the reasons behind the choices may matter. She has not decided that detail is bad. She has learned that the amount and order of detail should depend on what the reader is trying to do.

Day 77 · 日常生活 · 10 分鐘

The Map Facing the Wrong Way

比對方向與地標，修正視角造成的誤讀。

At a riverside walking path, Finn reads a map fixed to a board. The map shows north at the top, but the board faces west. Finn assumes that the top of the map means straight ahead from where he stands and starts toward the bicycle parking area.

His sister notices that the bridge should be on their right if they are following the planned route. Instead, it is behind them. They return to the board and compare the north arrow with two visible landmarks: the bridge and a tall red tower.

Once they understand the map's direction, they find the path to the visitor center. It is only a short walk, and they have not needed a new map. The problem came from how Finn connected the drawing to his own position.

Later, Finn sketches a small route for a friend. He marks both a north arrow and the starting point. He also labels the first landmark, giving the reader a way to check the route before walking too far in the wrong direction.

Day 78 · 對話／訊息 · 10 分鐘

The Interview We Can Actually Use

理解採訪問題與回答資料是否對應。

History group chat: Our talk asks why the old market matters to local residents. We will interview two shopkeepers tomorrow. Please ask about changes they have personally seen. We should distinguish their experiences from facts that need checking in the town records.

Nina: Can I ask whether the market is the oldest one in the county? Teacher: You can ask what they know, but one person's memory will not establish that claim. For the talk, check the official historical record before describing it as the oldest.

Bo: My first question is, Do you love this wonderful market? Nina: That sounds as if we want only a positive answer. How about, What do you value about working here, and what would you change?

Teacher: Better. Ask permission before recording, and offer to take notes instead. When using a quotation, keep its meaning intact. We can explain a mixed opinion without turning it into either complete praise or complete dislike.

Day 79 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

Which Surface Holds the Drop?

依描述判斷觀察指標與推論界線。

For a classroom observation, students place one drop of colored water on each of three surfaces: plain paper, waxed paper, and a plastic lid. They use the same dropper and try to make every drop the same size. A timer starts after each drop lands.

On plain paper, the wet mark spreads and becomes wider. On the other two surfaces, the water stays gathered into a small rounded drop during the observation period. Students sketch the shape at ten seconds and again at one minute.

Eva says that the plain paper must be weaker because its mark is larger. Her partner points out that the activity records how water behaves on a surface, not how much weight a material can hold. A spreading mark does not directly measure strength.

They decide to title the page Water on Three Surfaces and keep any strength question for a separate investigation. The pictures are useful because the students explain what was compared and when each observation was made.

The Community Story Wall

判斷投稿資格、字數與公開選項。

COMMUNITY STORY WALL: Share a memory of our neighborhood in one hundred to one hundred and fifty words. The memory should describe something you personally experienced. You may write in English or Chinese. Please avoid including another person's private contact details in your story.

Send your text by Friday evening. Volunteers may correct obvious spelling mistakes but will ask before changing the meaning. Selected stories will appear on the wall next month. Submission does not guarantee selection, and there is no entry fee or cash prize.

You may choose to show your first name or remain unnamed. Tell us your preference when submitting. Keep a copy of your original text because printed pages sent to the office will not be returned. Digital submissions are also welcome.

If a story mentions a living person in an identifiable way, check that they are comfortable with public display before submitting. For questions, visit the community desk on Tuesday afternoon. The volunteers can explain the process but cannot promise which stories will be chosen.

Day 82 · 單字與錯題復活 · 10 分鐘

The Words Behind a Clear Report

從資料用途推論字詞，練習精準表達。

The review club chooses five words: distinguish, strength, guarantee, preference, and agreement. Each student receives a sentence that is almost clear but still missing one important word. They must select a card and point to the part of the sentence that supports it.

One sentence compares a person's memory with a checked town record. Distinguish fits because the writer wants to tell the two kinds of information apart. Another says that a water mark does not measure how much weight paper can hold, which points to strength.

Preference belongs in a form asking whether the writer wants a first name displayed. Agreement fits a request to get the writer's approval before changing a story. Guarantee is used in a reminder that sending a story does not ensure selection.

Before checking, the students swap explanations without showing their chosen cards. A partner must guess the word from the reasoning alone. If the explanation fits several cards, they return to the original sentence and make the supporting clue more precise.

Day 83 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

The Shortcut in the Group Report

辨識資料來源可支持的結論範圍。

To describe how students travel to school, a project group asks everyone at its own lunch table. Seven of the eight students usually take a bus. Ken begins the report with the sentence Almost all students in our school travel by bus.

His partner points out that their table is mostly friends from the same neighborhood. Although the answers are real, the group has not asked students from other areas. Their method may leave out classmates who walk, cycle, or receive a ride from family.

They change the sentence to Seven of the eight students we asked usually take a bus. Then they plan to collect more responses from different classes, with a short explanation of how the participants are chosen. Each response will be counted only once.

The teacher does not ask them to hide the small survey. She asks them to label it accurately and avoid turning a convenient group into the whole school. The revised report is less dramatic, but its claim is easier to defend.

  3. Every student in the school.
  4. Only bus drivers.

  1. One.
  2. Six.
  3. Eight.

Day 84 · 日常生活 · 10 分鐘

The Restaurant List with One Review

判讀評論與個人需求，避免單一經驗過度推廣。

While planning a family lunch, Dean reads a restaurant review that gives one star because the meal arrived slowly during a festival. He nearly crosses the restaurant off the list. His mother asks him to check the review's date and the reason for the rating.

The family plans to visit on an ordinary weekday and needs a quiet table for six, including his grandfather. Dean finds the restaurant's current opening hours and calls to ask about seating. The staff offer a side room but say it must be reserved.

Dean also reads several recent reviews, which describe different waiting times. He does not decide that the old review is false. It reports one person's experience under particular conditions. He keeps it in mind while asking the staff how long weekday service usually takes.

They reserve the room and leave enough time before their next appointment. Dean learns to use reviews as pieces of information, alongside dates, circumstances, and the family's needs. A single rating is a starting point for questions, not a complete plan.

Day 86 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

A Chart with a Missing Afternoon

辨識缺失資料，避免把未測量當零。

The school garden team weighs collected leaves at the end of each afternoon. Their chart lists Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. The recorded amounts are two, three, blank, four, and one kilograms. A storm kept the team indoors on Wednesday, so no collection or measurement was made.

When making a weekly graph, Iris enters zero for Wednesday because the box is empty. Her partner asks whether zero means they measured nothing or did not measure at all. Those two situations may look similar on paper but mean different things.

They label Wednesday no measurement and keep the other four values. The total actually collected on the measured days is ten kilograms. They do not estimate Wednesday's possible amount without explaining a method and labeling it as an estimate.

The teacher asks readers what the chart can answer. It shows the recorded collection, but it cannot tell how many leaves fell across the whole week. Some leaves may have remained in the garden or blown away before the team returned.

  3. The team weighed exactly zero kilograms.
  4. No collection or measurement took place.

  1. Eleven kilograms.
  2. Ten kilograms.
  3. Four kilograms.
  4. Eight kilograms.

3 · 推論判讀 · 基礎

  1. Zero is not a number.
  2. It may imply a measurement that never occurred.
  3. Every blank must represent four kilograms.
  4. Wednesday was outside the school week.

4 · 字義推測 · 基礎

What is an 'estimate'?

  1. A label for every storm.
  2. An approximate value based on an explained method.
  3. The total of Friday's leaves only.
  4. An exact measurement automatically found in a blank.

5 · 資訊整合 · 進階

  1. The weight of leaves blown out of the garden.
  2. The amount the team recorded collecting on four days.
  3. The amount collected on Wednesday.
  4. The exact number of leaves that fell all week.

6 · 主旨統整 · 挑戰

What is the main lesson?

  1. Avoid labeling uncertain parts of a graph.

Day 88 · 每週 Boss · 15 分鐘

Boss: Arriving Before the Curtain

以不同交通方案的總時間決定可行選項。

SHOW DETAILS: A school play begins at six. Audience members must be seated ten minutes earlier. Tickets have already been collected online. Jo leaves home at five ten with her grandmother, who needs a level entrance and walks at the same pace used in the route estimates.

ROUTE CARD: Bus A leaves their stop at five fifteen, reaches the main gate at five thirty-five, and requires a twelve-minute walk around to the level side gate. Bus B leaves at five twenty and reaches the side gate at five forty-five.

ARRIVAL NOTE: From either side-gate arrival, allow five minutes to reach the seats. Walking from home to the bus stop takes four minutes. Neither bus requires a transfer. The route estimates already include ordinary traffic, but unexpected delays are still possible.

Jo compares the complete trips. She chooses Bus B because it reaches the level entrance directly and meets the seating deadline under the listed times. She keeps the school's contact number ready and avoids assuming that a bus's arrival at a gate means she is already seated.

Day 89 · 單字與錯題復活 · 10 分鐘

The Missing Number Review

用精確字詞描述紀錄、估計與時間限制。

The review club places five cards on the board: confirmation, estimate, level, transfer, and unexpected. Students must match them with short notes from a pretend journey. The teacher says the notes describe different kinds of information, even though they all belong to one trip.

A message from the ticket company accepting a date change is a confirmation. A travel time calculated from ordinary conditions is an estimate. A passenger changing from one bus to another makes a transfer. A flat entrance with no steps is level.

The final note describes a road closure that was not known when the plan was made. Students choose unexpected. One pair first uses estimate, but then notices that the sentence describes a new event rather than an approximate amount of time.

Before finishing, each student writes a question asking what remains uncertain after a booking is confirmed. The answers mention traffic and weather. A confirmed reservation does not confirm every detail of the journey, and the group underlines that distinction in its notes.

Day 90 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

A Role That Fits the Voice

以實際需求解讀分工，避免把選角當總能力評價。

When the class records an audio play, Ella wants the narrator's role because it has the most lines. She reads quickly and clearly, but the story needs a calm voice between noisy scenes. During practice, her classmate Ren naturally leaves useful pauses between sentences.

The group asks Ren to narrate and gives Ella a lively shopkeeper's role. Ella feels disappointed and assumes they think she is a poor reader. The director explains that choosing a voice for one role is not the same as ranking everyone's overall ability.

She plays two short recordings for the group and asks them to describe what each scene needs. Ella hears how the pauses help listeners follow a change of place. She also notices that the shopkeeper's quick speech makes the busy market sound convincing.

By the final recording, Ella enjoys her part and helps Ren pronounce a difficult name. The two students contribute different strengths. The group writes feedback about specific choices, so each actor knows what worked instead of receiving only a general label.

Day 91 · 日常生活 · 10 分鐘

Watering While They Are Away

整合每日表與例外條件，避免重複執行。

Before leaving for a three-day trip, the Wu family asks their neighbor Rosa to check two balcony plants. The instruction card says to check the soil each morning and water only if the top layer feels dry. It does not tell her to add water automatically every day.

Rosa's son reads only the heading Daily Plant Care and thinks both pots need a full cup each morning. Rosa shows him the sentence below it. One pot is already wet from overnight rain, while the other is sheltered under the balcony roof.

They mark a simple chart with checked, watered, or still damp for each pot. When Mr. Wu sends a message offering to ask another neighbor for help, Rosa replies with a photo of the chart so the same job will not be done twice.

At the end of the trip, the family thanks Rosa for following the conditions, not just the heading. The chart makes clear that checking daily and watering daily are two different instructions, even when they appear on the same card.

Day 92 · 對話／訊息 · 10 分鐘

A Faster Practice, or a Shorter One?

比對運動紀錄的距離與時間，避免只看數字大小。

Running club chat: I finished today's practice in twelve minutes, two minutes faster than last week. I think my speed has improved a lot. The message includes a photo of a watch, but no route description or distance is shown beside it.

Coach: Was today's route the same length? Runner: Last week we used four laps of the track. Today the inside lane was closed, so we ran three laps and then stopped at the side gate. I did not measure the final distance.

Coach: Then the shorter time alone cannot show a faster pace. Record distance as well as duration next time. You can still note that you completed today's planned session; just avoid comparing two different routes as if they were equal.

Another teammate offers to draw the next route and mark its start and finish. The group agrees to keep weather and any interruptions in their notes too. A useful record gives enough context for a comparison, rather than only the most impressive number.

Day 93 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

Seeds on the Wool Square

辨識樣本觀察與普遍結論的差距。

After walking beside a field, Mira finds several small hooked seeds attached to her socks. For a classroom demonstration, she brings collected seeds and three equal-size surfaces: wool cloth, smooth plastic, and plain paper. She does not collect new seeds from the protected school garden.

The class gently presses ten seeds against each surface once, then lifts the surface. Seven remain on the wool, one on the plastic, and two on the paper. Students count only seeds still attached after the surface is held upright for ten seconds.

One student says the test proves every seed travels on wool. Mira points to the hooked seeds in their sample. They have not tested other shapes, and the pressing method is only a simple demonstration, not a record of every trip through a field.

The class draws the hooks and the cloth fibers they can see. They suggest that these features help explain this result, while leaving room for another test. Their report names both the sample and the procedure so another group can try the same activity.

Day 96 · 單字與錯題復活 · 10 分鐘

Before, After, and Enough

在新情境中辨別期限、時長與預留時間。

For the weekly review, five cards read duration, procedure, subtitles, combined, and buffer. The last word is new, so the teacher adds a clue: a few spare minutes between finishing lunch and catching a bus. This extra time can absorb a small delay.

The group uses duration for how long a show lasts. Procedure belongs beside the steps for collecting tickets. Subtitles are written words on the screen, while a combined ticket covers two named programs under one purchase. Students explain each match with a short example.

A second exercise gives a plan that ends at exactly the bus departure time. It fits the listed times but has no buffer. One student wants to call the plan guaranteed. Her partner asks what would happen if ordering lunch took two extra minutes.

The group writes two separate judgments: mathematically possible under the stated times, but sensitive to delay. They keep that wording because it says more than simply good or bad. A precise explanation should show both what works and which condition could change the result.

Day 97 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

The Phone Box Exception

追蹤一般規則與經核准的例外。

In Class Nine, phones usually stay in a numbered box during lessons. A notice says students may retrieve a device for a learning task only when the teacher gives permission. The rule is meant to reduce interruptions without preventing a planned activity that needs a camera or timer.

During a science lesson, Dan sees Mina using her phone and says she is breaking the rule. Mina has been asked to photograph the group's model. Dan did not hear the instruction because he was helping carry materials from the storage room.

Instead of arguing about what must have happened, Dan asks the teacher to clarify. She explains the limited permission and reminds Mina to return the device after taking the pictures. The permission does not allow unrelated messaging during the rest of the lesson.

Later, the teacher writes the approved task and its ending point on the board. Dan apologizes for making a public accusation before checking the situation. A general rule still matters, but applying it fairly requires knowing whether a specific exception has actually been authorized.

Day 98 · 日常生活 · 10 分鐘

A Birthday in Two Calendars

核對日期來源與溝通方式，避免替人猜測。

Rae plans a surprise meal for her grandmother and finds two different birthday dates in the family chat. One message says March twelve, while another lists a date in a traditional calendar. Rae assumes one message must be wrong and begins correcting everyone's calendar entries.

Her uncle asks her to pause. The family sometimes uses different calendars, and a traditional-calendar birthday does not necessarily fall on the same date in the calendar printed on Rae's phone each year. They need to confirm which celebration date her grandmother prefers this time.

Instead of asking directly about a surprise party, Rae checks with her mother, who has already discussed the year's plan with her grandmother. The family agrees on the Saturday lunch that suits her. Rae sends one clear message naming both the date and the day of the week.

She also labels it celebration meal rather than official birthday date. That distinction helps relatives understand what is being arranged. The meal succeeds because Rae verifies the plan, not because she wins an argument about which old message looked more certain.

When the Practice Moves Indoors

Band chat: We plan to practice in the courtyard tomorrow at four. If rain is falling at three thirty, we will move to Room 102. Please check the teacher's message at that time. A morning forecast alone will not decide which space we use.

Felix: The weather app shows rain, so I told my friend to go straight to Room 102. Leader: Please correct that message. The room is only our backup until the teacher checks the conditions. We want everyone to use the same final instruction.

At three thirty, the teacher posts: It is raining now. Use Room 102 and bring only instruments that fit through its narrow doorway. Large drums will stay in the music room, and we will practice their parts with a small drum instead.

Felix forwards the complete message rather than only the room number. He adds that tomorrow's outdoor plan remains unchanged unless a new notice appears. The group now knows today's location, the equipment adjustment, and where to look for the next update.

Day 100 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

Two Bins, Different Groups

辨認比例的分母，避免只比件數。

During a school waste-sorting activity, two classes inspect their recycling bins before collection. Class A finds twenty correctly sorted items out of twenty-five. Class B finds twenty-four correctly sorted items out of forty. The classes use the same sorting checklist and count each item once.

A student says Class B did better because twenty-four is larger than twenty. Another asks to consider how many items were checked in each class. Having more correct items does not necessarily mean a larger share of the bin was sorted correctly.

Class A's share is eighty percent, while Class B's is sixty percent. The report includes both counts and percentages. It describes only the bins examined on that day, since neither group has kept a long-term record of its usual sorting habits.

Both classes choose one common mistake from their own bin and make a clearer label for the following week. The goal is to improve decisions at the bin, not turn one small check into a permanent label about which class is more responsible.

The Workshop Deposit

Day 104 · 校園故事 · 10 分鐘

A Practice Plan with One Hard Bar

理解練習策略與回饋證據的關係。

During band practice, Inez can play most of a short piece smoothly, but one difficult bar keeps interrupting the melody. She starts from the beginning each time she makes a mistake. After twenty minutes, she has played the easy opening many times and the hard bar only a few.

Her teacher suggests marking the troublesome notes and practicing that bar slowly. Inez then adds the bar before it and the bar after it, so the difficult movement connects with the rest of the piece. She records a short attempt rather than the whole rehearsal.

On playback, she hears that the notes are now correct but the pause before them is too long. She works on the transition and records again. This time she listens for the specific pause instead of simply deciding whether the entire performance feels good.

At the end, Inez plays the complete piece once. She still has work to do, but her notes describe exactly what improved and what needs another attempt. Focused feedback has turned a vague feeling of failure into a manageable next step.

Day 105 · 日常生活 · 10 分鐘

The Price on the Small Card

辨識一次性費用與持續費用，計算指定期間總額。

Two printing shops advertise notebook-binding services. Shop Green charges thirty dollars to set up a design and ten dollars for each bound notebook. Shop Blue has no setup fee but charges fifteen dollars per notebook. Both use the same paper that the customer supplies.

Riko needs eight notebooks for a club gift project. A friend says Green must be more expensive because its sign shows an extra thirty-dollar fee. Riko writes down both complete calculations instead of comparing only the largest number on each small advertisement.

Green's total for eight notebooks is one hundred and ten dollars. Blue's is one hundred and twenty. Riko confirms that the setup fee is paid once for the shared design, not once per notebook. She also asks whether the quoted totals include all binding charges.

The club chooses Green for this order. Riko does not conclude that Green is cheaper for every order size. With fewer notebooks, the one-time fee could change the comparison. She saves the two price rules, not merely today's winning shop name.

Day 106 · 對話／訊息 · 10 分鐘

The Quote with a Missing Sentence

核對引述前後文，分辨刪節是否改變原意。

Newsletter chat: I want to quote the librarian saying, The new reading room is too small. It will make a strong opening for our article about the renovation. The quote comes from the interview we recorded yesterday after getting her permission.

Editor: What did she say next? Writer: She said, It is too small for large group talks, but it works well for quiet individual reading. She also suggested keeping group events in the old hall because that space has movable chairs.

Editor: Then quoting only the first sentence could make readers think she dislikes the room for every use. Include the condition about large groups and her positive point about individual reading. A shorter quote should still preserve the view she expressed.

Writer: I will introduce both uses and check the recording again before publication. We can ask whether the layout fits each activity instead of deciding that the whole room is simply good or bad. The headline should reflect that question too.

Day 107 · 科普閱讀 · 10 分鐘

The Sunlit Cloth Squares

判斷資料可支持的結論及未控制變因。

In a classroom scenario, a team compares two cloth squares under a sunny window. One is black cotton and the other is white cotton. The squares have the same size and thickness. The teacher places a temperature sensor beneath each and starts the observation together.

After fifteen minutes, the reading under the black square is thirty-five degrees Celsius, while the white square reads thirty-one. Both began at twenty-eight degrees. The group records the starting and ending values instead of reporting only the higher final number.

They repeat the comparison after switching the squares' left and right positions. This helps them check whether one part of the windowsill receives different sunlight. They keep the same observation time and use the same two sensors throughout the activity.

The first round suggests a difference under these conditions, but the team avoids a claim about all black and white objects everywhere. Other materials, locations, or weather could change the results. The report includes the setup so readers can understand what the numbers actually compare.
